target_customer: Gastroenterology practices and endoscopists performing colonoscopies
problem: Endoscopists miss polyps and struggle to capture quality metrics and documentation; Docbot applied AI to detect polyps in real time and automate procedure data capture and billing.
business_model: Healthcare software sold to GI practices, funded by seed capital and an NSF SBIR grant while pursuing clinical trials

founders.name: Andrew Ninh
founders.background_notes: Listed as CEO in the UCI release; YC lists him as a founder.

founders.name: Tyler Dao
founders.background_notes: Listed by YC; no background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time computer vision on endoscopy video needs labeled clinical data, low latency integration with hospital video systems and eventual FDA clearance.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical data and regulatory clearance would be hard to replicate, but clearance had not been obtained and larger device makers had similar programs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Medtronic's GI Genius (from Cosmo) won the first FDA authorization for AI polyp detection in 2021; Docbot's assets and some staff were bought by Satisfai Health in November 2022.

market_need_then: Colonoscopy miss rates were a known clinical problem and AI assisted detection had published trial interest; the company reported use in about 6,000 procedures by 2019 per its release and about 2,000 per the 2022 acquirer release.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic doctor plus bot name shared with unrelated chatbot products; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Docbot raised about 2.0M USD in seed funding and a 225K USD NSF grant in 2019 to run polyp detection trials, but never reached FDA clearance as far as public sources show. In November 2022 Satisfai Health bought its intellectual property and assets and took on key technical staff, which looks like an asset sale. Medtronic's GI Genius took the first FDA authorization in 2021. The lack of a later round is inferred, not sourced.
notes: No company website is listed in the directory, so there was no site to fetch. CB Insights shows Series A and 4.47M USD total, unverified and not recorded. The first search wrongly suggested an ambient documentation product; the UCI and acquirer releases show it was GI computer vision. Procedure counts differ between sources. No dated competitor sources from early 2019 were found; GI Genius was authorized in 2021 and is recorded in takeover risk only. Satisfai is also spelled Satisfy in some sources. Founder roles beyond Ninh and Karnes are unsourced.
